transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been noticing a pattern in the project files for months. Certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making small changes to the translation memory and the timestamps, so it ends up looking like my quality control failed. IT says the audit trail is clean, but I don’t think it is. I think the records have been arranged to put the blame on me.
Have you heard any voices, whispers, or noises when no one else was around?
No, I haven’t noticed voices or whispers when I’m alone.
How has your mood been over the past few weeks—have you been feeling down or depressed?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed. I’ve been frustrated and preoccupied with what’s going on, but I wouldn’t describe myself as feeling down most of the time.
Do you ever feel that outside forces or other people are putting thoughts into your mind or controlling your actions?
No. I don’t feel like anyone is putting thoughts in my head or controlling what I do.
Aside from what is happening at work, do you find it hard to trust the people close to you, such as friends or family?
No, not really. I generally trust my friends and family.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F60.0 as mistrust is not pervasive across settings (trusts friends and family), and ruled out F20.0 due to absence of hallucinations, thought passivity/insertion, or bizarre delusions.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a circumscribed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion involving coworkers manipulating work files and timestamps to sabotage their performance, which has persisted for months despite objective contradictory evidence from IT. There are no auditory or other hallucinations, thought insertion/passivity phenomena, affective syndromes, or pervasive interpersonal mistrust indicative of paranoid personality disorder.

confirmed_symptoms: Fixed persecutory belief that colleagues and subcontractors are deliberately altering work files and timestamps to falsely assign blame
Belief persists despite IT confirmation that the audit trail is normal
Absence of thought insertion or external control phenomena
Absence of prominent depressive or affective episodes
Absence of pervasive paranoia outside of the specific circumscribed work situation

additional_requirements: Absence of organic brain disease or substance-induced etiology
